environment.description: Same application deployed on AWS ECS Fargate behind an ALB with the following configuration: (1) ALB HTTP listener has a fixed-response rule that strips requests containing both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length headers simultaneously (rule priority 1, condition: http-header 'transfer-encoding' exists AND http-header 'content-length' exists → fixed-response 400). (2) CloudFront distribution in front of ALB with a Response Headers Policy that injects Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net 'sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self' — this CSP with SRI hash means only the exact known-good middleware.js script (matching the sha384 integrity value) can execute, blocking any attacker-controlled cdn parameter from loading tampered scripts. (3) CloudFront also normalizes chunked encoding by fully buffering request bodies before forwarding, eliminating TE/CL desync at the ALB layer.

config.alb_rule: priority-1: reject requests with both TE and CL headers (fixed-response 400)
config.cloudfront_request_policy: full body buffering, HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 normalization
config.sri_enforcement: CSP script-src with sha384 integrity hash for known-good script
